images.title: Fold in three, then in half
images.purpose: Set up the question: fold a 1 unit strip into 3 equal parts, then fold the folded strip in half; how many equal parts are there now?
images.composition: The opened strip in three parts on the left and the folded three layer stack on the right, with wide space between, and one question line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Left: one strip, 1 unit long, split by 2 grey #6B7280 creases into 3 exactly equal parts, filled teal #0072B2. Right: the same strip folded into 3 equal layers stacked like the letter S, filled amber #E69F00, with one dashed reddish purple #CC79A7 line across its middle showing the next fold. One question line centred below. Exactly 1 opened strip, 2 creases, 1 folded stack, 1 dashed fold line.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any fraction written in the frame, or a strip opened after the second fold
images.takeaway: Every part is folded in two; count the parts on the opened strip.
images.description: A 1 unit strip with 2 creases making 3 equal parts, and the strip folded into 3 layers with a dashed line where it will be folded in half, under the question How many parts now?
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say what happens to each of the 3 parts when the stack is folded in half.

image_decisions.why: Showing the strip in three parts and the folded stack with the next fold line gives the cue without the opened result.
